observed_product_context.candidate_semantics_under_test: snapshot mutable one-byte C-contiguous memoryview with memoryview.tobytes() into owned bytes
observed_product_context.note: The experiment is a mechanism discriminator for the candidate ownership contract; it is not exact-current-main product acceptance.

grf.observed_reality: The current Bytes candidate copies a mutable admitted memoryview into a new bytes object, while earlier project evidence already rejected readonly-view as proof of immutable backing provenance.
grf.generated_reality: An owned copy could be sufficient to define a stable Clay Bytes value even if the exporter remains mutable, because post-copy producer mutations cannot mutate the returned bytes object.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: If the producer can mutate shared memory concurrently while the copy is in progress, the resulting owned bytes object can be a torn/mixed state that never corresponded to a single producer epoch; ownership-after-copy does not itself establish snapshot consistency or provenance-stable ingress.
grf.discriminating_prediction_hypothesis: Every copied 4 MiB snapshot during alternating whole-buffer A/B producer epochs is internally homogeneous ALL_A or ALL_B.
grf.discriminating_prediction_counterhypothe: At least one copied snapshot is MIXED_AB while the producer updates the shared buffer in halves.

unusual_experiment.intervention: A separate process alternated the same shared mmap between A and B in two half-buffer writes with a bounded pause between halves while the candidate snapshot operation copied the full memoryview.
unusual_experiment.rollback: Ephemeral sandbox stopped; temporary mmap file deleted by the experiment; no canonical product source was mutated by the experiment itself.

interpretation.supported_claim: memoryview.tobytes() provides owned immutable result storage but does not by itself guarantee a producer-epoch-consistent snapshot when the backing shared memory is concurrently mutated
not_supported: that all mutable buffers require copying
that zero-copy can never be safe
that Clay Bytes semantics are now selected
that whole EntityOS or Clay Machine acceptance passed
interpretation.required_contract_delta: For concurrently mutable/shared exporters, define and test an explicit producer lease/epoch/stability handshake, versioned immutable publication protocol, seqlock-like validated retry, or another mechanism that proves the admitted bytes correspond to one declared producer epoch. Fail closed or snapshot through a validated protocol when stability cannot be established.
interpretation.performance_followup: Any retry/copy/lease design must be measured for latency, throughput, copy count, allocation pressure and starvation under sustained writer activity before CM-DATA performance claims.

next_falsifiers: Implement the smallest versioned epoch-before/copy/epoch-after retry oracle and prove it never admits MIXED_AB under the same writer intervention.
Bound retry/starvation behavior under a continuously mutating producer and fail closed after a declared budget.
Carry the selected stability metadata through typed Clay Bytes/Buffer -> executable TypedIR -> single ClayVM ingress without backend-local semantics.
